CSTEP Training · for the CSTEP Admin and Officials

Arrange tours, settle them, and verify claims

Once a request is approved it comes to you. For a tour, the Official books each service with a vendor and records the payment, the traveller reports back after the trip, and the Office settles it. For a claim, the CSTEP Admin checks every line against its bill and sends the net amount to Finance.

Part 1 of 4

Arrange a tour

The Official books what an approved tour needs — one line per service.

  1. 1Your processing queue
  2. 2Open the tour — arranging starts
  3. 3Pick the vendor per line
  4. 4Details, amount, Mark arranged
  5. 5Payment: Paid or Pending
  6. 6Mark arrangements complete
ArrangeStep 1 of 6 · Your queue

Processing — every case you are responsible for

Travel Claims → Approvals opens Your Queues. As an Official you see the Processing list, by stage: Tour Request (approved, to arrange), Arrangement in Progress, Arranged, Tour Report in Progress, Report Submitted, Transferred to Finance, Settled, Reimbursed.

Each card shows the TIN, Tour approved, the route, project, dates and traveller. Review opens it.

Travel Claims → ApprovalsTour RequestReview
ArrangeStep 2 of 6 · Open the tour

Opening it starts arranging

Opening an approved tour moves it to ARRANGING (the audit trail records START_ARRANGING).

What was arranged has one line per service the traveller asked for — here Flight, Cab and Hotel — each with Details, Amount, Mark arranged and a Vendor. Add service adds anything else.

ArrangeStep 3 of 6 · Vendor

Choose the vendor

Choose a vendor lists the active vendors from the Vendor Master — the ones whose type suits the service come first under Suggested (airlines for a flight), then All vendors. Type to search by name, code, city or type.

Until a line has a vendor it says Needs a vendor before it can be paid.

Choose a vendorSuggested first
ArrangeStep 4 of 6 · Arrange each line

Details, amount, Mark arranged

For each line enter the details (flight numbers, times, room, dates) and the amount, then click Mark arranged — it turns Arranged ✓. Each field saves as you leave it.

Every line with a vendor now shows its payment status: Payment pending, with Mark paid.

VendorDetails · amountMark arranged
ArrangeStep 5 of 6 · Payment

Mark paid — the payment reference

When a vendor has been paid, Mark paid opens three fields: the UTR / cheque no., the vendor's invoice no. (optional) and the payment date. Then Save payment.

Finance can also do this in bulk from Vendor payments — see the Finance deck.

ArrangeStep 5 of 6 · Payment

Paid or Pending, line by line

The flight now shows Payment done with its UTR, date and invoice number; the cab and hotel are still Payment pending.

A paid line is locked — Mark unpaid first to change its vendor or amount.

ArrangeStep 6 of 6 · Complete

Mark arrangements complete

When every service is booked, Mark arrangements complete: the tour is ARRANGED. The audit trail records MARK_ARRANGED, and each vendor payment (VENDOR_PAYMENT) with its reference.

The traveller now sees what was arranged — and, after the trip, files their report.

Part 2 of 4

The traveller's post-trip report

What the traveller files after the trip — the record the settlement is built from.

  1. 1Back from the trip?
  2. 2Legs seeded from the arrangements
  3. 3A document on every leg
  4. 4Self-paid costs and extra legs
  5. 5Submit report
ReportStep 1 of 3 · Back from the trip

Back from the trip? File the report

On the traveller's request page, under what was arranged, Back from the trip? — File post-trip report: every leg, with its supporting document.

It is the traveller's own step; nothing files it for them.

ReportStep 2 of 3 · Legs

Legs seeded from what was arranged

Onward Journey Particulars starts with one leg per arranged service, marked Booked by CSTEP, with its fare and details.

A warning lists every leg still missing a document — Submit report stays disabled until there are none.

ReportStep 2 of 3 · Legs

Places, dates, documents — and what they paid themselves

For each leg: from, to and the dates, and Upload the boarding pass, voucher or receipt. Add legs with + Add a leg to Onward / Return — here the return flight.

A cost the traveller paid is marked Self Paid, Receipt Attached with its fare — here a ₹640 local cab. That is what they are reimbursed for.

From · to · datesUpload a document per legSelf-paid: fare + receipt
ReportStep 3 of 3 · Submit

Report submitted

Submit report (they confirm — it can't be edited afterwards): status REPORT SUBMITTED, recorded as SUBMIT_REPORT.

The page now offers the packet — View Packet / Download Full Packet: the formal record with every document. It goes to the Official to settle.

Part 3 of 4

Settle the tour

The Office (Accounts / Admin) checks every line, sets the per diem, and finalizes.

  1. 1Report Submitted in your queue
  2. 2Per diem
  3. 3Verify every expense line
  4. 4The totals
  5. 5Finalize — to Finance
SettleStep 1 of 5 · Your queue

Report Submitted

The tour moves to Report Submitted in the Official's Processing queue.

Review opens it at the settlement.

SettleStep 2 of 5 · Settlement

Step 5 · Settlement

For Office (Accounts / Admin) purposes only. The Per Diem row counts the days from the trip dates (here 3) × a rate per day.

Expense lines lists everything: each arranged service (Arranged by CSTEP) and each leg from the report — with its amount, Official / Personal, the document to Open, and Verify.

SettleStep 3 of 5 · Verify

Per diem rate, and every line verified

Enter the rate per day (here ₹800 → ₹2,400). Overriding the days asks for a reason.

Check each line against its document, correct an amount if needed, and click Verify. Official means CSTEP paid it; Personal means the traveller paid and is owed it back — changing either asks for a reason.

SettleStep 4 of 5 · Totals

The buckets and the amount claimed

The lines roll up into Air / Train / Bus, Per Diem, Boarding & Lodging, Cab and Other.

Total Cost of Tour is everything (₹26,280 here); Amount Claimed is what the traveller is owed — the per diem plus what they paid themselves (₹3,040). Send back to traveller returns the report to fix.

SettleStep 5 of 5 · Finalize

Finalized — sent to Finance

Finalize settlement (confirm) makes it read-only: ₹3,040 owed → sent to Finance, who reimburse the traveller. If nothing is owed it closes instead.

Every line keeps its verified mark and classification on record.

Part 4 of 4

Verify claims

The CSTEP Admin checks an approved claim line by line before Finance pays it.

  1. 1Claim verification queue
  2. 2Check each line against its bill
  3. 3Correct an amount
  4. 4Verify & send to Finance
  5. 5An Expense Claim: the tax invoice
Verify claimsStep 1 of 6 · Your queue

Claim verification

As CSTEP Admin, Your Queues has a tab per stage — Approvals, Processing, Claim verification, Finance and Vendor payments — and counts claims to verify.

To verify lists approved claims with their reference (LTC…, EXP…). Review opens one.

Travel Claims → ApprovalsClaim verificationReview
Verify claimsStep 2 of 6 · Check the lines

Claim verification — every line

For CSTEP Admin purposes only. Each claim line with its amount, Official / Personal (a claimant's own spend starts as Personal — owed back to them), its document — or No document for a no-bill trip on the declaration — and Verify.

Underneath: the amount claimed, less any advance, and the amount due by CSTEP.

Verify claimsStep 3 of 6 · Correct & verify

Correct an amount, verify each line

Change an amount that doesn't match its bill — here the lunch, ₹210 → ₹200 — and the totals follow (₹975).

Verify each line; the counter reads 3 / 3 verified.

Check against the billCorrect the amountVerify each line
Verify claimsStep 4 of 6 · Send to Finance

Verify & send to Finance

Verify & send to Finance sends the net amount for reimbursement: Verified → with Finance. (When nothing is due the button reads Verify & close.)

The lines are now read-only.

Verify claimsStep 5 of 6 · Expense Claim

An Expense Claim — against the tax invoice

An Expense Claim lists each expense and the tax (IGST) as lines — Open shows the attached tax invoice.

Check every line and the tax against the invoice, verify each, then Verify & send to Finance.

Verify claimsStep 5 of 6 · Expense Claim

Verified — with Finance

2 / 2 verified and Verified → with Finance: ₹6,372 due by CSTEP goes to Finance.

Verify claimsStep 6 of 6 · With Finance

Everything now waits on Finance

The Finance tab now holds all three — the two claims and the settled tour — Sent to reimbursement.

From here the Finance user reimburses; that is the next deck.

Reference

Who does what after approval

The steps in this deck, in order.

StepWhoWhereEnds with
Arrange the tourOfficial (or CSTEP Admin)Approvals → Processing → Tour RequestARRANGED — every line with a vendor; payments Paid / Pending
Post-trip reportThe travellerTheir request → File post-trip reportREPORT SUBMITTED — a document on every leg
Settle the tourOfficial / Office (Accounts, Admin)Processing → Report SubmittedFinalized: amount owed → Finance, or closed
Verify a claimCSTEP AdminApprovals → Claim verificationVerified → with Finance (or closed when nothing is due)
Recap

From approval to Finance

Arrange
A vendor on every line, details and amount, Mark arranged; record each payment as it is made.
Report
The traveller reports every leg with a document; self-paid costs carry their receipt.
Settle
Per diem, verify every line (Official = CSTEP paid, Personal = owed back), finalize.
Verify claims
Check each line against its bill or the invoice, correct, verify, send to Finance.
